answer_1.quote: Recent studies have applied LLMs to script-related tasks, demonstrating that these models have scripting knowledge... we propose the Agent-Based Script Evaluation Framework (ABSEval) to evaluate the scripts.
answer_1.outputs: Generated step-by-step scripts for real-life tasks

answer_2.quote: Automated evaluation methods like BERTScore and Rouge assess script correctness by calculating semantic similarity ... we compare ABSEval to BERTScore and Rouge.

answer_3.quote: We propose the Agent-Based Script Evaluation Framework (ABSEval), an evaluation system that integrates Answer Synthesize Agent, Critic Agent, Execute Agent and Commonsense Agent to comprehensively evaluate the scripts.
methods: Answer Synthesize Agent generates gold answer
Critic Agent compares scripts to gold answer
Execute Agent executes steps to check goal and constraints

answer_4.quote: We randomly selected 200 scripts generated by LLMs for manual annotation... A better evaluation would obtain results similar to those obtained by human annotations.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators marked yes/no for each script on seven criteria: missing steps, redundant steps, duplicate steps, goal completion, constraint satisfaction, correct order, and commonsense consistency.
